description: Per-BUS-machine identity facts that no other SSOT file states: which ERP `machine_ref` a machine's production orders are booked under, and whether the id is a second protocol view of a machine already present under another id (a MIRROR). WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: both facts were hard-declared in consumer code (i3x-v4 services/golden-shift/src/machine-identity.ts) because the SSOT had no place for them. That is exactly the drift this repo is supposed to prevent — a machine's identity is a property of the machine, not of whichever service happens to need it. SOURCE→BUS aliasing is NOT here: it is already derivable by joining a source descriptor's `machineId` with the `source.sourceRef` of a `sync/nats/*` mapping, and a fact that is already derivable must not be restated. EVERY entry carries the measurement that established it. An identity justified by name similarity alone is a bug even when it happens to be right: `sgm-006` books as `sgm-06` and `cnc-mtc-02` books as `cnc-03`, neither of which a leading-zero rule would produce. A machine with NO proven ERP ref belongs here with `erpMachineRef: null` — the consumer then leaves the order binding absent and greys the hour, which is the honest outcome. It must never guess something close. Validated by ci/lint-machine-identity.mjs against the source descriptors and sync mappings.

evidence.measured: ERP emits cnc-001 directly since the 2026-07-07 zero-pad flip (business_events: slug cnc-01 ends 2026-07-20, cnc-001 starts 2026-07-07). Article-correlation control: top match is cnc-001 (10.5%, runner-up 3.7%).
ERP emits cnc-002 directly since the 2026-07-07 flip (slug cnc-02 ends 2026-07-20). Article-correlation control: top match is cnc-002 (6.8%).
ERP emits sgm-001 since 2026-07-07 (slug sgm-01 stops the same day — a clean flip). Article-correlation control: top match is sgm-001 (3.1%).
ERP emits sgm-004 since 2026-07-07 (slug sgm-04 stops the same day). Article-correlation control: top match is sgm-004 (6.2%).
ERP emits sgm-005 since 2026-07-07 (slug sgm-05 stops the same day).
ERP emits rockwell-01 directly (business_events 2026-07-20..2026-07-29). Article-correlation control: top match is rockwell-01 (23.2%).

TWO independent ground truths agree, the same pair the 2026-07-07 zero-pad rule was established on. (1) PHYSICAL: the source endpoint is opc.tcp://192.168.178.154:36065; the machines-sgm range starts at 36060 = sgm-001, so 36065 = range start + 5 = sim machine #6 = slug sgm-06. (2) DATA: article correlation over 2103 currentProgram events gives sgm-06 as the top machine_ref (6.3%; the only other entry above noise is the POOL-SGM dispatch bucket at 4.7%).

machines.note: sources/opcua/opcua-sgm-006-processdata.json describes this machine as 'v4-SGM-012'. The v4 token is explicitly NOT authoritative (2026-07-07 rule) and is off by one — MTConnect device sgm-01 is described 'v4-SGM-002'. Both measurements above say sgm-06; the description string should be corrected in osf-schemas.

evidence.measured: Article correlation, run in BOTH directions with the base rate controlled (Jaccard over (article, hour) sets, ERP restricted to status in_arbeit). cnc-mtc-02 → cnc-03 is a MUTUAL BEST PAIR: forward rank #1 (10.32 vs runner-up 4.49), backward rank #1 (cnc-03 → cnc-mtc-02, 10.32 vs runner-up 3.90). A raw ±5min hit count agrees: cnc-03 rank #1 at 54/731 (7.4%), runner-up 2.5%. Under the same base-rate-controlled test all six machines whose ref is independently known return their own ref at rank #1 in both directions (cnc-001 8.63/4.34, cnc-002 6.86/4.75, rockwell-01 20.04/6.14, sgm-001 3.91/2.42, sgm-004 7.98/5.51, sgm-005 3.22/1.81) — the control that makes this verdict usable.

machines.note: CORRECTION to an earlier claim of mine: I first cited sources/mtconnect/mtconnect-cnc-mtc-02.json's connection.device = 'cnc-03' as an INDEPENDENT confirmation of the ERP ref. It is not. The MTConnect agent's device namespace is NOT the ERP machine_ref namespace — agent devices cnc-11..cnc-14 are the machines ERP books as HB600P/HB760/HB1000P/HB1500-1, and ERP carries cnc-11..cnc-20 as separate refs besides. The cnc-mtc-01 chain proves the device id can mislead outright (declared device cnc-01, measured identical to cnc-002). That the device id and the ERP ref coincide here is therefore a finding, not a second source; the ERP ref rests on the correlation above alone.

evidence.measured: Value-level identity with cnc-002, not a name match: over 2026-07-20..2026-07-26 the machine-specific Act_Amount_PartGood counter agrees on 5363 of 5364 co-timed samples (99.98%), while the same test against cnc-001 gives 0/4898 and against cnc-mtc-02 gives 9/4793. Act_Ref_Program agrees on 894/895 co-timed samples. A part counter is per-machine and monotonic — identical values mean one physical machine sampled twice.

machines.note: sources/mtconnect/mtconnect-cnc-01.json and sources/opcua/opcua-mtbridge-cnc-01.json declare this chain as MTConnect agent device 'cnc-01' and warn that agent device cnc-02 is 'unrelated' to the OPC-UA machine cnc-002. The counter measurement contradicts that: the machine behind this chain IS cnc-002. Which end is mislabelled (the Sonder-Edge polling a different device than declared, or the descriptor's identity note) needs a look at the Sonder-Edge config, which is not in our SSOT.

evidence.measured: Value-level identity with rockwell-01: over 2026-07-20..2026-07-23 Act_Amount_PartGood agrees on 1449 of 1450 co-timed samples (99.9%), while the same test against cnc-001 gives 0/1032 and against cnc-002 gives 0/762. Article correlation independently puts rockwell-01 top for ftlinx-01 at 36.7%.
